articles.summary: Acadia Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Nasdaq: ACAD), today announced that it has entered into an exclusive distribution agreement with KYORIN Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (TSE: 4569), for the commercialization of DAYBUE ® STIX (trofinetide) powder for oral solution in Japan for the treatment of Rett syndrome. Under the terms of the agreement, KYORIN will be responsible for leading the commercialization of DAYBUE STIX in Japan and the related regulatory activities on behalf of Acadia. Acadia will receive an upfront payment of $30 million and is eligible to receive future regulatory and sales milestone payments as well as a share of net sales of DAYBUE STIX in Japan. Acadia recently completed a Phase 3 study of trofinetide in Japan, with results consistent with the pivotal LAVENDER™ Phase 3 study. “KYORIN’s commercial expertise and established presence in Japan make them an ideal partner to bring DAYBUE to patients and families living with Rett syndrome,” said Catherine Owen Adams, Chief Executive
articles.title: Acadia Pharmaceuticals Enters Exclusive Distribution Agreement with KYORIN Pharmaceutical for DAYBUE® STIX (trofinetide) in Japan

articles.summary: Acadia Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Nasdaq: ACAD) today announced that it will present two data presentations related to Alzheimer's disease psychosis (ADP) and remlifanserin at the 2026 Clinical Trials on Alzheimer's Disease (CTAD) conference, taking place November 16-19, 2026, in Boston. Acadia's presentations include an oral presentation featuring findings from the Phase 2 portion of the ongoing RADIANT clinical trial program evaluating remlifanserin in patients with Alzheimer's disease psychosis, as well as a poster presentation examining biomarker heterogeneity among patients meeting clinical criteria for ADP. Collectively, these presentations reflect Acadia's commitment to advancing the understanding and treatment of psychosis associated with Alzheimer’s disease. articles.summary: Acadia Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Nasdaq: ACAD) today reported that oral arguments were held before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit in the appeal of the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware’s May 2025 decision upholding Acadia’s U.S. Patent No. 11,452,721 (the ‘721 patent), which covers the NUPLAZID® (pimavanserin) 34 mg capsule formulation. “We continue to believe in the strength of our position on the NUPLAZID formulation patent, on which the Federal Circuit heard oral arguments today,” said Catherine Owen Adams, Chief Executive Officer of Acadia. “Acadia believes the district court’s decision is supported by the facts established at trial and by applicable law. The trial court decided key issues of fact after hearing detailed testimony from experts.
